scenario: A Citizens roof inspection of a 2004 single-family house in Ocala, Florida, carried out for a renewal. The house has two roof surfaces: an architectural shingle dwelling roof replaced in full in 2020, and a standing-seam metal roof over the rear addition partially replaced in 2023 after a hail event.
notes: Every ourField the published map names has a value here. A checkbox field takes one of the whenValue strings that field's own boxes carry — the slug vocabulary (yes / satisfactory / full_replacement), not the sentence the form prints. The renderer refuses an answer no box carries, so a value written the wrong way stops the form rather than producing a blank.

⚠️ PAGE 1 IS NOT A BACK COVER. Eight of these values live there — the whole signature block plus Additional Comments — and a value set written by the four-point form's habit of stopping at the page before the last would leave every one of them unexercised. They are listed last, and they are the reason this file has 36 entries rather than 28.

The twelve roof blanks are about 41.5pt wide and every overlay on this form declares both a maxWidth and a maxHeight, so fit.ts measures each one: a value too long is refused rather than wrapped down over the row beneath. The dates and covering materials here are written the abbreviated way an inspector writes them on paper because that is what the blank holds.

Both roof slots are filled although a house with one roof would fill only the first. This file exists to put a value through every mapping, and an empty slot proves nothing about the coordinate underneath it.

The signature block's date is inspector_signature_date. This form prints a single word, 'Date', under a certification sentence, and the notes beside the candidate record why it is read as the signing date rather than a second inspection date: the visit is already dated on page 0.
This is invented data about an invented property. Nothing here is a record of a real inspection, and no value is a real person, licence number, policy number or address.
Read by scripts/verify-statutory-render.mjs. Correct a value in place; nothing generates this file.

values.additional_comments: The dwelling roof is architectural shingle, replaced in full under permit in 2020, with granule loss consistent with age and no soft decking underfoot. The rear addition carries a standing-seam metal roof; about a fifth of the panels were replaced in 2023 after hail, and the remainder show shallow dents on the south-facing slope with no perforation and no coating loss. No staining was found at the attic underside or at any interior ceiling.
